public_rationale: Marcus forecast, with no date, that in the long term we will all have our own AI agents and companies will have armies of them. The only evidence item is a Salesforce earnings release. It reports more than 9,500 paid Agentforce deals as of the quarter ending 31 October 2025, up 50% from the prior quarter. That shows company agent use growing. It does not show large companies routinely running many agents. The packet has no data on how many people use a personal AI agent. So the early-support rule is not met. The packet also has no evidence of a lasting collapse of agent use, which is the only thing that could count against the forecast early. With no deadline, the forecast stays open.
limitations: The packet has no population-level data on personal AI agent use.
The Salesforce figures cover one vendor. They do not show how many agents each company runs or how common agent fleets are across companies.
Words like 'all' and 'armies' are loose, so any future test would need a reasonable threshold.
A McKinsey survey on agent adoption could not be loaded and was not used.

statement.document_title: AI Agents: Hype versus Reality, redux

from_speaker: we will all have our own AI agents
companies will have armies of them
this time I think the hype is right — at least in the long term
our_interpretation: Read as a long-term forecast with no deadline: most people will use a personal AI agent, and companies will deploy agents in large numbers.
He set no date. 'In the long term' means this cannot fail before some distant, unstated point.
criteria.support_condition: Credible adoption data show that personal AI agents are used by most people, and that companies commonly run large fleets of agents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, this cannot be contradicted on a fixed date. Only a decisive event, such as agents being abandoned or banned at scale, would count against it.
